legal.draftNotice: Draft for the test system: this text has not been reviewed by the provider's legal team and is not the final version. The final text will be published before launch.

sections.title: What this service is
sections.body: Nitimitr provides general legal information based on the system's knowledge library to help you understand your situation. It is not legal advice for your specific case. The system is not a lawyer, does not argue cases, and does not represent you before any court or agency.

sections.title: Accuracy of information
sections.body: Answers show their sources and the date of the information so you can check the original. Each item in the library shows its real review status; content that has not been reviewed by a content reviewer is marked as a draft. Laws change, so verify against the original before relying on it.

sections.title: Urgent and high-risk matters
sections.body: For matters with a deadline, involving arrest, violence, or large sums, speak to a lawyer or a legal-aid organisation directly. The system shows a warning and help channels when it detects such a matter.

sections.title: Acceptable use
sections.body: Do not use the system for anything unlawful, try to break into it or make it unavailable, or upload other people's data without the right to do so. Trial (guest) users can send a limited number of messages per day, and their data is deleted as described in the privacy notice.

sections.title: Account and security
sections.body: Keep your password secret. The system locks an account temporarily after several wrong passwords and signs you out after a period of inactivity. You can turn on two-step verification, see signed-in devices and delete your account yourself in Settings.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
sections.body: When the terms change, you will be asked to read and accept the new version before continuing.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: The provider and contact channels will be published in the final version before launch.

sections.title: Data we keep
sections.body: Email, display name, password (only a hash is stored, never the password itself), the questions you ask and the answers in each conversation, feedback you give on answers, settings, consent records, and security data such as a hash of your IP address and browser type.

sections.title: Purposes
sections.body: To provide Q&A and keep your conversation history, and for account security and audit. The system does not currently use your data for marketing. Any other use in future would ask for separate consent.

sections.title: Sending data to external services
sections.body: Your question is searched in the system's own knowledge library. If the library has no answer, the system may send the question to the service provider's company knowledge-base service for supplementary information, after ID-card numbers, phone numbers, bank account numbers and e-mail addresses are masked. Raw conversation text is not written to the system's application logs.

sections.title: Retention
sections.body: Guest data is deleted after {guestHours} hours without use. When you request account deletion, a {graceDays}-day grace period starts, during which you can cancel by signing in. After that your account, conversations and settings are permanently deleted.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can export your data as a file, request account deletion and see your consent records yourself in Settings > Privacy. You have the right to complain to the Personal Data Protection Committee as provided by law.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Each organization's data is kept separate. Back-office staff must use two-step verification. Important changes are recorded in an audit log.

sections.title: Controller and contact
sections.body: The data controller and the data protection contact will be published in the final version before launch.
